summary: Feed s142_double to NDR is degraded: 11.6% duplicate packets waste capacity and 51.1% of TCP sessions are one-way, preventing stateful NDR detection. No truncation, drops, overload, VLAN or encryption issues detected.

findings.root_cause: 51.1% of TCP sessions (67/131) are single-direction, well above 10% threshold. NDR requires both directions but is only seeing one side. Most likely packet broker is not aggregating both directions to this tool port - e.g., asymmetric routing with single-sided SPAN/TAP, or per-packet load-balancing splitting client->server and server->client across different outputs, or TX-only SPAN.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly, flow state and attack detection. With only one direction it cannot reconstruct sessions, misses lateral movement/exfiltration, creates incomplete flows and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR port using flow-aware (5-tuple) hashing/aggregation so the NDR sees complete bidirectional sessions for detection.

findings.root_cause: 11.6% of packets (206/1775) are duplicates, exceeding 5% threshold. Indicates overlapping capture sources (e.g., SPAN + TAP on same link, or both sides of a TAP aggregated without deduplication) and packet broker forwarding both copies to the NDR without deduplication.
findings.impact_on_tool: Duplicates waste NDR 10G port bandwidth and processing, inflate flow/packet counters, skew analytics and can cause false detections or mask real anomalies while reducing effective detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (hash-based, ~10ms window) to suppress duplicate copies before delivery to NDR, preserving capacity for unique traffic.
